scenes.heading: Hydrocarbons and organic families
scenes.sub: Sorting millions of carbon compounds into a few families
scenes.say: Petrol, plastics, vinegar and hand sanitiser are all carbon compounds. There are millions of them, so how do chemists keep track? They sort them into families.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A train adding one carriage at a time
scenes.science: A homologous series: each member is one CH₂ longer
scenes.breaks: real carbon chains zigzag in 3D and can branch, which changes properties even with the same number of carbons.
scenes.say: Picture a train where each new version has one more carriage. In a homologous series, each member is one C H two unit longer than the last: methane, ethane, propane, butane. They all react the same way, but each extra carriage makes the molecule heavier, so boiling points rise gradually.

scenes.heading: Counting carbons
scenes.say: The start of the name tells you how many carbons are in the longest chain. Remember Mother Eats Peanut Butter for meth, eth, prop and but: one to four. Then pent, hex, hept and oct, like a pentagon, hexagon and octagon. And every carbon always makes four bonds.

scenes.heading: Saturated vs unsaturated
scenes.say: Alkanes are saturated: only single bonds, with the general formula C n H two n plus two. They're fairly unreactive, so we mostly burn them as fuels. Alkenes have a double bond, with the formula C n H two n. The double bond can open up, so alkenes do addition reactions and are used to make plastics.
scenes.caption: Alkanes are saturated: only single bonds, with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. They're fairly unreactive, so we mostly burn them as fuels. Alkenes have a double bond, with the formula CₙH₂ₙ. The double bond can open up, so alkenes do addition reactions and are used to make plastics.

scenes.heading: Family endings
scenes.say: The ending tells you the family. Y N E is an alkyne, with a triple bond. O L is an alcohol, with an O H group. Oic acid is a carboxylic acid. And oate is an ester, named alcohol part first, acid part second, like ethyl ethanoate.
scenes.caption: The ending tells you the family. -yne is an alkyne, with a triple bond. -ol is an alcohol, with an –OH group. -oic acid is a carboxylic acid. And -oate is an ester, named alcohol part first, acid part second, like ethyl ethanoate.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Name CH₃CH₂CH₂CH(OH)CH₃.
lines: Number from the end nearer the –OH: C2
scenes.say: Let's name this one. The longest chain has five carbons, so it's pent. There's an O H group, so it's an alcohol, ending in O L. Number from the end closer to the O H, which puts it on carbon two. So the name is pentan-2-ol.
scenes.caption: Let's name this one. The longest chain has five carbons, so it's pent-. There's an –OH group, so it's an alcohol, ending in -ol. Number from the end closer to the –OH, which puts it on carbon 2. So the name is pentan-2-ol.

scenes.say: Quick recap. Each member of a homologous series adds one C H two. The prefix counts carbons and the suffix names the family. Alkenes are unsaturated and do addition reactions. Longer chains have higher boiling points. Now try the practice questions!
